# Browser use and co-browsing

> Browser sessions are the `kind="browser"` case of
> [co-desktops](/features/computer-use). The same manager, control lease
> and activity trail now also drive Linux desktops, Windows/macOS VMs and remote
> VNC/SSH machines.

Browser use gives every chat a real Chromium browser that **you and the AI
share**. It is not an AI-only headless browser and not a second "user browser":
there is one page, one history, one cookie jar and one live view.

## What you can do

- Open a browser session from **Coworking** or from a chat and watch the
  page live while the AI works.
- Click, type, scroll and navigate directly in the live view; the AI sees the
  same page on its next tool call.
- Ask the AI to navigate, click, fill forms, run JavaScript, read the page text,
  list links, take screenshots, inspect the HTML source, or review what the user
  did recently.
- Hand control back and forth explicitly. The AI pauses when the human types or
  clicks in the live view, and can request a handoff for login/MFA/captcha.
- Keep the browser profile (cookies, logins, local storage) across restarts.
- Save and replay per-site scripts in one tool call instead of one LLM turn per
  step.
- **Record a flow in the coworking screen** — do "Create a post" once, stop the
  recording, and the generated steps become a recipe the AI can replay. Record
  over an existing recipe to update it (the old version is archived).

## Architecture

```text
                   codx-junior_default Docker network
 ┌────────────────────┐        CDP (port 9223)        ┌──────────────────────┐
 │  API / SmolAgent   │ ────────────────────────────► │  Chromium container  │
 │  Playwright        │                               │  ┌────────────────┐  │
 └─────────┬──────────┘                               │  │ CDP proxy      │  │
           │                                          │  │ 9223 → 9222    │  │
           │ REST / Socket.IO                         │  └────────────────┘  │
 ┌─────────▼──────────┐      Traefik route            │  ┌────────────────┐  │
 │  User browser      │ ────────────────────────────► │  │ Selkies VNC    │  │
 │  live view iframe  │      /browser/<id>/           │  │ port 3000      │  │
 └────────────────────┘                               │  └────────────────┘  │
                                                      └──────────────────────┘
```

- **User control / viewing** — the LinuxServer.io Chromium image exposes a
  Selkies web desktop. Traefik routes it at `/browser/<session_id>/`; the
  session is configured with `SUBFOLDER` so all assets and websockets work
  behind the path prefix.
- **AI control** — Chromium binds DevTools to `127.0.0.1` and rejects non-local
  `Host` headers. A tiny in-container proxy (`cdp_proxy.py`) listens on
  `0.0.0.0:9223`, rewrites the header and tunnels the connection to
  `127.0.0.1:9222`. Playwright connects to the proxy over the shared Docker
  network; both actors therefore drive the **same page**.
- **Persistence** — the container mounts
  `.codx/browser_sessions/<session_id>/chromium_profile` at `/config`.
- **Runtime** — the API keeps one Playwright connection per session (idle
  disconnect after 5 minutes) and serializes actions with a per-session lock.
  A 1-second watcher drains the in-page recorder, so human clicks/edits/tab
  switches show up as `actor=user` activity without polling the whole log.
- **Navigation** — `domcontentloaded` plus a short best-effort `load` wait;
  `networkidle` is no longer used (it timed out on live sites and the old code
  navigated a second time).

```js
// Minimal, dependency-free behavioural test for the docs site.
// Run: node --test qa/   (from the repository root, i.e. docs/)
// Rationale: .vitepress/config.mts sets ignoreDeadLinks: true, so a green
// `vitepress build` proves nothing about links. This test fails instead.

import { test } from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join, resolve } from 'node:path'

const CONFIG = '.vitepress/config.mts'

function findRoot(start = process.cwd()) {
  let dir = resolve(start)
  for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
    if (existsSync(join(dir, CONFIG))) return dir
    const parent = resolve(dir, '..')
    if (parent === dir) break
    dir = parent
  }
  throw new Error(`cannot find ${CONFIG} above ${start}`)
}

const root = findRoot()
const configSource = readFileSync(join(root, CONFIG), 'utf8')
const links = [...configSource.matchAll(/link:\s*'(\/[^']*)'/g)].map((m) => m[1])

function target(link) {
  const clean = link.split('#')[0].split('?')[0]
  if (clean === '' || clean === '/') return join(root, 'index.md')
  const rel = clean.replace(/^\//, '').replace(/\/$/, '')
  const candidates = [join(root, `${rel}.md`), join(root, rel, 'index.md')]
  return candidates.find((p) => existsSync(p) && statSync(p).isFile()) ?? candidates[0]
}

function markdownFiles(dir) {
  return readdirSync(join(root, dir), { withFileTypes: true })
    .flatMap((entry) => {
      const rel = `${dir}/${entry.name}`
      if (entry.isDirectory()) return markdownFiles(rel)
      return entry.name.endsWith('.md') ? [rel] : []
    })
}

test('every nav and sidebar link resolves to a markdown file', () => {
  assert.ok(links.length > 20, `expected the sidebar to declare links, found ${links.length}`)
  const broken = links.filter((link) => !existsSync(target(link)))
  assert.deepEqual(broken, [], `dead links: ${broken.join(', ')}`)
})

test('every published page is reachable from the config', () => {
  const pages = [...markdownFiles('features'), ...markdownFiles('guide')].filter(
    (p) => p !== 'features/index.md'
  )
  const published = (page) => {
    const slug = page.replace(/\.md$/, '')
    return (
      configSource.includes(`'/${slug}'`) ||
      configSource.includes(`'/${slug}/'`) ||
      configSource.includes(`'/${slug}.md'`)
    )
  }
  const orphans = pages.filter((page) => !published(page))
  assert.deepEqual(orphans, [], `published but unreachable: ${orphans.join(', ')}`)
})
```

request.name: Two internal P0 design reviews are published on the public docs site (`/features/workspaces-*-review`) — disclose-and-fix, exclude them from the VitePress build
request.description:
Found while drafting the first behavioural test for the docs project (card `09e338b9`, 2026-11-19 ~11:10Z).

## The problem

VitePress publishes every `.md` under the docs root. `.vitepress/config.mts` (120 lines) sets `ignoreDeadLinks: true` but **has no `srcExclude`**. Two files that are internal engineering reviews therefore sit at live public URLs and no page links to them:

| file | lines | live URL | inbound links |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| `features/workspaces-container-routing-review.md` | 827 | `/features/workspaces-container-routing-review` | 0 |
| `features/workspaces-settings-scope-review.md` | 588 | `/features/workspaces-settings-scope-review` | 0 |

The first one is a **vulnerability disclosure**, not just an internal note. Its §3 "Blocking findings (P0)" states, in public:

- `P0-6. Proxied apps are not authenticated` (line 202)
- `P0-1. Workspace creation always fails` (line 65)
- `P0-2. There is no lifecycle API`, `P0-4. Workspace files are not persistent or host-visible`, `P0-5. Traefik cannot reach workspace containers`, `P0-7. Project admins have no path through the API`, `P0-8. Custom workspaces never receive Traefik labels`

plus §5 "Target design", §6 "Change list by area", §7 "Phased delivery" — an unreleased remediation plan. The second file is the same class (target model, API changes, migration plan).

`ignoreDeadLinks: true` is why nobody noticed: the build is green and the pages are simply never surfaced.

## Why it is urgent

The 19 Nov approval (`a8be6182`) is deciding the `features/` diff and the docs site is the public artefact. Every further commit makes this harder to unpublish quietly.

## What to do (minimal)

1. `.vitepress/config.mts`: add `srcExclude: ['features/*-review.md']` (or move both files under a non-published folder such as `docs-internal/` if they must stay in the tree). Excluding is the smaller change and reversible.
2. Decide on `features/channel-creator.md` in the same pass: it is published and has zero inbound links (in neither the sidebar nor `features/index.md`) — link it or exclude it.
3. Once `09e338b9` lands, its test 2 ("every published page is linked, or excluded") goes green with this change and fails again if a future review doc is added without an exclusion — i.e. this becomes a permanent gate, not a one-off cleanup.

## Acceptance criteria

- Neither URL renders from a `docs:build` output (check the built `dist/` for the two paths).
- `features/*-review.md` still readable in the repository.
- Any decision recorded in a comment here, with the resulting `git diff --stat` for `.vitepress/config.mts`.

## Constraints

Do **not** fold this into the pending approval diff while the 19 Nov verdict is unanswered — a new unowned file is exactly what invalidated that baseline twice. If a decision is needed sooner, it is an exclusion line in `config.mts`, nothing more.
